title: Book One · Chapter 38: The Name in the Shirt
story:
A month passes after the class display. The boys fly the kite on two dry afternoons. It stays by the door on wet days. Ronan often walks past it now. He does not stop for a check each time.

Mum's sewing pile changes every week. Mum finishes some repairs. People bring her more clothes. Some have torn knees. Mum needs to fix some sleeves. She needs to put buttons on other clothes.

On Saturday, she puts three shirts on the bed.

“Each shirt needs a name on its bag,” she says.

“I can make names,” Ronan offers.

“You can help me write the labels. I'll check them and pin them on.”

She gives him three paper strips. Ronan can copy the first name easily. The second name is harder. Ronan turns some of its letters the wrong way. The third label is for Mrs Lan's white shirt.

He writes LAN very carefully. He knows that name now. Mrs Lan lives at the front. She keeps the gate hook shut. She opens the hook for visitors.

Mum reads all three labels. Mum stops at one name. “Look at the middle,” she says. Ronan checks his copy. He missed a small letter. Now it says a different name.

“Will this name bring the wrong person?” he asks.

“Maybe not. But the name on my record must be right.”

He crosses the name out and copies it again below. Mum doesn't ask him to make a beautiful new label. The clear corrected one is enough.

Then she writes the work beside each name: pocket, two buttons, sleeve. Ronan draws a tiny pocket on the first strip.

“Can I draw all the jobs?”

“Beside the words. I still need the words.”

Mum starts sewing. Ronan puts spare buttons in a low dish. He sorts them by colour. One red button looks like an eye. He opens his school book to the cat picture. He puts the red button on it. The real cat stays outside.

Mrs Lan comes to the door. “That cat can see enough already. It does not need a big red eye!”

Mrs Lan asks about a loose stitch in her shirt. Mum shows her the work. “Tomorrow afternoon,” she says. “I can finish it then.” Mrs Lan can wear a different shirt that morning.

Mum does not promise the shirt for breakfast. Some jobs take a long time. Mum is still learning. Her eyes get tired at night. Then she puts her needle down.

Dad brings bread home for lunch. He still has no regular work. “Do you have enough sewing customers now?” Dad asks.

“A few,” Mum says. “Not enough to say more than that.”

He nods. Ronan eats beside them. Mum and Dad talk about thread costs. Mum buys buttons for her jobs. Then she puts them on the clothes. She also has to buy thread. Some of her pay goes on these things. She can spend the rest on the family.

After lunch, Ronan takes the labels to his school bag by mistake. He opens his reading book. There are the labels.

He carries them back at once.

“I moved the names, not the shirts,” he says.

Mum puts the labels back in the work box. “I need these names for the shirts. Thank you. You brought the labels back in time.”

He laughs, but he checks the names with her again. She folds a little cloth over each pin. Then the strip stays in place. His help took more time today. Mum checks the last name with him. “Now all three labels are right,” she says. Ronan leaves the box beside her chair.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：labels＝标签；stitch＝针脚；buttons＝纽扣；customers＝顾客。

辅助理解：pin作动词表示用别针固定；sew表示缝。

理解问题：

1. Mum 为什么在衣服上加标签？
2. Ronan 的帮助在哪一步需要重新检查？
